SRAN|M40001C0.Description: Average value of Voltage Standing Wave Ratio over the whole measurement period.   Valid VSWR samples are converted to their RC (reflection coefficient) equivalents. Converted values are summed up and the sum is divided by the number of valid samples  for the measurement period. The average RC value is converted back to average VSWR value.  The counter is cleared at Radio Module reset, or when unit is lost.  If the average could not be calculated (for example, there were no valid readouts during the  measurement period) the counter for that period is not distributed.

SRAN|M40100C0.Measurement Name: Loose Phase and Time Sync Statistics
SRAN|M40100C0.Measurement ID and Name in previous rele: Loose Phase and Time Sync Statistics
SRAN|M40100C0.Description: The minimum value of the measured raw BTS time error against time reference source in milliseconds during the interval, in loose phase and time synchronization. Note: The raw BTS time error does not contain external factors, such as maximum assumed variation of the external time reference input signal over time (which is configurable parameter only for NTP [maxNtpTimeError]), nor safe margin applied due to phase drifting over time (as there is no phase synchronization anymore after start-up but only frequency synchronization). Hence the counter presents purely the BTS capability to follow loose time reference.

SRAN|M51300C1.Description: Number of received Ethernet frames where the EtherType does not match to any Ethernet application. NOTE:The criteria of counting will vary according to operation mode (e.g. VLAN, PPPoE). PPP/PPPoE mode: - EthTypeMismatch counter of ETHIF is incremented for each ingress frame, where Ethertype is not 0x8863 or 0x8864, (incremented also for VLAN tagged frames).  Ethernet mode: - EthTypeMismatch counter of ETHIF is incremented for each untagged or priority-tagged (TPID=0x8100 for Ethernet C-tag, VLAN-ID=0) ingress frame, where (inner) Ethertype is different than IPv4 or ARP, but not incremented for VLAN-tagged frames (TPID=0x8100 for Ethernet C-tag, VLAN-ID<>0) - EthTypeMismatch counter of VLANIF is incremented for each VLAN-tagged (TPID=0x8100 for Ethernet C-tag) ingress frame, where "inner" Ethertype is different than IPv4 or ARP.

SRAN|M51303C0.Description: Unavailable Seconds (UAS): Counts the number of seconds for which the interface is unavailable. The interface is defined to be unavailable from either the beginning of 10 contiguous SES, and/or a defect. An interface is available again after a 10-second absence of all defects and SES. While the interface is unavailable, the only count that is incremented is UAS. Defect: LOS, LOF, AIS.
SRAN|M51303C0.Description in previous release: Unavailable Seconds (UAS): Counts the number of seconds for which the interface is unavailable. The interface is defined to be unavailable from either the beginning of 10 contiguous SES, and/or a defect. An interface is available again after a 10-second absence of all defects and SES. While the interface is unavailable, the only count that is incremented is UAS. Defect: LOS, LOF, AIS.
SRAN|M51303C0.Updated: The counter is incremented for every second when the interface is in a period of unavailable time. SRAN|M51329C1.Description: All received ESP packets addressed to a local tunnel endpoint which are received with an SPI of an existing IPsec SA but being discarded because they are considered as replayed packets are counted. If standard sequence numbers (32 bit) are used, then packets with sequence number below the lower edge of the anti-replay window or packets with sequence number within the anti-replay window but being previously received are considered as replayed packets. If 64 bit Extended Sequence Numbers (ESN) are used then only the latter condition applies. In the ESN case only the lower 32 bit are included in the packet header, whereas the upper 32 bit are determined on sender’s and receiver’s side by means of a specific scheme outlined in RFC 4303. The complete 64 bit ESN is also used on both ends to calculate the Integrity Check Value (ICV). Because of the ESN scheme there are certain cases where packets are replayed but cannot be classified as such by the receiver (see RFC 4303 for details). These packets fail the integrity check and therefore are classified and consequently counted as cryptographic errors.
